reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis that Ti addition increases stacking fault energy (SFE) in CoCrFeNiTi contradicts the well-established trend that Ti generally lowers SFE in Ni/Co-based alloys, making the core mechanistic assumption physically questionable.
reasons.testability: The proposed in-situ TEM and interrupted tests with a Ti-free baseline provide a clear, direct way to measure dislocation mobility and dynamic recovery, and the falsification criteria are well-defined.
reasons.usefulness: Despite being physically unsound, the hypothesis is highly useful because it frames a clear, testable mechanistic contrast (SFE-driven vs. other mechanisms) that would advance understanding of deformation in this alloy system.
